title: Recombinant adeno-associated virus mediated gene delivery in the extracranial nervous system of adult mice by direct nerve immersion
protocol: Anesthetize the adult mouse using an inhalation agent such as isoflurane.
Confirm deep anesthesia by pinching the tail or paw with unserrated forceps.
Apply ophthalmic ointment generously onto both eyes of the mouse.
Prepare the surgical area on the upper hindlimb.
Administer injectable anesthesia consisting of 75 mg/kg ketamine and 1 mg/kg medetomidine (optional).
Provide subcutaneous fluid administration for postoperative care if using injectable anesthesia.
Place a heating pad under the cage to maintain body temperature during surgery if using injectable anesthesia.
Spray the fur along both hindlimbs with 70% ethanol.
Remove the fur on the upper hindlimb using a scalpel or an electrical rodent shaver.
Extend the fur removal area from slightly below the knee up to the hip region.
Mark the skin incision site for surgery.
Disinfect the surgical area with an iodine-containing solution (e.g., betadine).
Wait for 15 seconds until the applied betadine is dried on the skin.
If betadine is not accessible, use 70% ethanol as an alternative.
Expose the trifurcation site of the sciatic nerve.
Dissect the dermal layer proximal to the knee joint with a scalpel.
Make a small (approximately 3–5 mm) longitudinal incision in the dermal layer.
Carefully separate the muscle layer close to the femur by blunt dissection with a pair of scissors.
Reveal the trifurcation site of the sciatic nerve.
Expose approximately 5 mm of the nerve structure above and below the trifurcation site.
Briefly vortex the freshly thawed aliquot of AAV particles for about 3–5 seconds.
Aspirate the desired volume of AAV suspension (2–10 μL) with a filtered pipette tip.
Gently open the separated muscles using an unserrated forceps.
Drop-wise apply the AAV suspension onto the sciatic nerve trifurcation site without touching the nerve.
Load the pipette with AAV suspension while the surgeon performs nerve exposure.
Minimize the risk of exposed nerve becoming dry by immediate muscle closure post-application.
Avoid repetitive touching of the nerve during the procedure.
Do not insert any foreign material into the incision to restrict diffusion of AAV solution.
Gently appose the muscle layers for approximately 10 seconds with the tip of an unserrated forceps.
Close the skin wound using a veterinarian approved tissue adhesive (or alternatively sutures).
Inject an analgesic solution subcutaneously post-operatively according to national and institutional guidelines.
Monitor the mouse for approximately 2 hours after returning it to its home cage for signs of discomfort and pain, such as restricted mobility, shivering, and vocalizations.
House the mice in your animal facility for 3–6 weeks post-procedure.
Euthanize the mouse according to institutional guidelines.
Create a similar intramuscular space by blunt dissection.
Collect the trunk of the sciatic nerve extending from its emergence at the sciatic notch to the trifurcation in the popliteal fossa behind the knee joint.
Dissect and collect a piece of biceps femoris muscle (50–100 mg) using forceps and small scissors.
Dissect and collect a small piece (50–100 mg) of liver using forceps and small scissors as a control tissue for gene and/or protein expression studies.
Isolate dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and spinal cord tissue as illustrated previously.
Process the collected tissue(s) for gene and/or protein expression analysis.
Perform microscopy on the processed tissues.
Conduct desired assays relevant to the research interest.
